edits.hypothesis: Replaces the rejected benchmark-specific exact-match grader rules with a reusable extractive-QA procedure: resolve the reference, choose the shortest verbatim context span matching the question's requested form, emit only that span, then self-check for extra tokens. This generalizes to unseen supplied-context QA tasks and cites no grader, task IDs, or specific answers.

Embedding a six-case emission contract in CLAUDE.md makes the minimal-span, full-name, full-sentence, yes/no, and measurement rules available on every turn, even if the answer-verifier skill is skipped or unavailable, so the fixed model is more likely to emit only the exact requested span.

Adding explicit extraction rules for A-or-B questions, first-name-before-'and', no grammatical-form rewriting, and fuller title/name spans corrects recurrent selection and span-boundary errors with reusable rules rather than task constants.

Strengthening the verifier with a replace-with-closest-exact-span step plus dimension and grammatical-form checks gives the second verification pass concrete corrective instructions, reducing overinclusion and normalization errors after drafting.

Replaces the previous per-question-type decision tree with one reusable extractive-QA procedure: form focused, phrase, and full-sentence candidates from the single answer-bearing sentence, then choose the shortest verbatim candidate that passes a grammatical completion test, does not repeat question words, and does not split a compound expression. This is a general span-calibration mechanism rather than a set of task-specific carve-outs.

edits.hypothesis: A general emission contract with reusable linguistic categories (count, classification, measurement, definition/record, named entity, place, relation, fallback) keeps span-boundary guidance available on every turn without dataset-shaped patterns such as named prior answers or fixed question templates.

A focus-first verifier with explicit keep/drop calibration is a reusable extractive-QA safeguard: it rejects non-substring drafts, preserves required head nouns and proper-name qualifiers, and prevents importing a fuller name form from a different context entry.

Reusable reference-resolution rules in the question-answering skill, plus a verifier check that rejects a merely-substring answer belonging to the wrong subject, address anaphora and A-or-B selection without task-specific constants.

Remove the incumbent measurement-unit rule that pulled count questions toward `number + unit` and replace it with a reusable numeric-answer rule: `How many` keeps only the numeral unless the question names a standard measuring unit; other measurement questions keep a unit only when it is a standard measure. This removes the instruction that previously led the model to append a counted noun while still allowing genuine `How many [unit]` measurement answers.

Remove the incumbent `fullest continuous form` person/title rule and make the sentence that directly states the requested fact the authority for person and titled-work spans: copy that sentence's exact name/title form, do not import forms from other entries, and when the question names alternatives choose the shortest context occurrence of the supported alternative. This is a reusable reference-resolution and span-boundary rule, not a per-task correction.

Replace the incumbent shortest-place-name trimming guidance with a reusable locative/proper-noun span-boundary rule: for place, company, organization, and other proper-noun answers keep the full contiguous phrase as written in the answer-bearing sentence, including suffixes and comma-separated locations, and drop only a leading locative preposition; for relation/route questions keep the leading relation word. This is motivated by observed span-boundary errors rather than by any specific task or answer.

Embedding focus-specific count/classification/where/relation/statement emission rules in the always-present CLAUDE.md makes the span-boundary correction available on every turn even if a skill payload is skipped or unavailable, reducing the dominant short_answer_overinclusion failures with reusable linguistic categories and no task constants.

A verifier that forms HEAD, PHRASE, and SENTENCE candidates from the answer-bearing sentence and then selects by question focus is a reusable second-pass correction mechanism: it catches both over-trimmed class phrases and over-expanded class labels after drafting, without referencing any task or answer.

Replacing the incumbent 'fullest continuous form' name/title rule with an answer-bearing-sentence rule that keeps the shortest exact name/title still identifying the answer, preserves question-named alternatives, and returns the descriptive role for who-is-X questions corrects recurrent canonical-name and title span overextension without task-specific constants.

An always-present focus-first emission contract removes the incumbent 'fullest continuous form' and bare-shortest-span rules, replacing them with reusable linguistic boundary rules for count, classification, award, place, relation, measurement, and event questions so the model emits only the requested span even if a skill payload is skipped.

The drafting skill resolves references first and calibrates person, title, organization, and place answers to the exact form in the answer-bearing sentence, while rejecting fuller forms imported from other entries and later adaptations; this is reusable span-boundary behavior, not task-specific constants.

The verifier now compares the draft with the answer-bearing sentence and applies focus-specific span checks, catching both over-inclusion and under-extraction after drafting; this closes the reported answer-bearing-span capability gap without any task-specific answers.

Restores the general shortest-complete-span and strip-qualifier protection to the always-present prompt, replacing benchmark-specific examples with a reusable procedure: resolve to the answer-bearing sentence, choose the shortest verbatim span that still fills the answer slot, and strip only question-redundant tokens without splitting compound expressions. This keeps span calibration available on every turn even if a skill payload is unavailable.

Makes the question-answering skill the single source for reusable focus-boundary rules: after resolving the question to the single answer-bearing sentence, the model copies the exact name/title/proper-noun form from that sentence and applies linguistic focus rules (count, classification, relation, measurement, statement). This replaces task-derived examples with reusable categories and preserves the explicit bridge-reasoning habit.

Makes the verifier an independent second pass that reconstructs the answer-bearing sentence, applies the general shortest-complete-span check first, and then corrects the boundary according to the question focus. Because the general check is primary and the focus rules are reusable linguistic categories with no task-specific examples, it catches both over-trimmed class phrases and over-trimmed place phrases after drafting.

Replaces the rejected biographical-entry exception with a coherent person-name boundary rule in both skills. For a who/which-person question the model copies the name from the sentence that states the identifying description (the phrase that would replace who/which), never shrinks to a bare surname, and does not add a middle name or quoted nickname from another sentence. The general no-import checks now explicitly defer to this Person rule, so the mechanism no longer contradicts itself.

Mirrors the same coherent person-name boundary rule in the always-present CLAUDE.md prompt and adds an explicit exception to its general no-import instruction, so the corrected person-name behavior is available even if the skill is skipped.
